entries.label: Agent
entries.help: Agent runtime configuration.

entries.label: Approval Mode
entries.help: Tool approval mode.

entries.label: Streaming
entries.help: Enable streaming responses.

entries.label: Model
entries.help: LLM model identifier. 'auto' resolves from agent config.

entries.label: Per-role models
entries.help: Optional per-task-class model overrides. Keys: 'background' (lite / heartbeat background workers) and 'subagent' (spawned sub-agents). An empty value or 'auto' defers to the chat default (agent.model) and then to the provider default, so an unpinned role stays usable on every subscription tier. Pin a cheaper model here to run background / sub-agent work on it without changing the interactive chat default.

entries.label: Per-role reasoning effort
entries.help: Optional per-task-class reasoning effort, paired with role_models (keys: 'background', 'subagent'). Empty for a role inherits the chat default (agent.reasoning_effort) and then the provider/model default. Only applies on reasoning-capable models.

entries.label: Reasoning Effort
entries.help: Default reasoning effort for new sessions on models that support it. Empty defers to the provider/model default. Per-session overrides win.

entries.label: Provider
entries.help: LLM provider backend (KiroACP / kiro-cli).

entries.label: Default Agent
entries.help: Default agent name for new sessions.

entries.label: Sandbox
entries.help: Sandbox mode for ACP provider. Default 'off' defers isolation to kiro-cli's internal agent sandbox (kiro-cli >= 2.13). Set to 'auto' to re-enable Kiro Crew's OS-level sandbox (namespace on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS). The two layers are mutually exclusive on macOS (nested seatbelt causes EPERM).

entries.label: Allow No-Isolation Fallback
entries.help: Acknowledge running the agent subprocess WITHOUT OS-level credential isolation when no sandbox backend is available (e.g. macOS >= 26, or Linux without user namespaces). When false (default), that fallback is logged as a loud SECURITY warning. When true, the operator has accepted the risk and it is logged at info level.

entries.label: Allow Unsandboxed Execution
entries.help: When true, allow agent subprocesses to execute without any sandbox backend (fail-open). When false (default), wrap_argv raises a RuntimeError if no sandbox backend is available and mode is not 'off', preventing unsandboxed execution entirely (fail-closed). This is distinct from sandbox_allow_no_isolation which only controls warning severity — this field controls whether execution proceeds at all. The default is platform-independent: on a host with no backend (any Windows host, a Linux kernel refusing user namespaces) `kirocrew setup` OFFERS this opt-in interactively and writes it only on an explicit yes, so unconfined execution stays operator-declared and is never enabled implicitly by the platform.

entries.label: Allow Third-Party Apps
entries.help: Explicitly allow executable code from third-party (non-builtin) apps. Defaults to false. Only the JSON boolean true admits in-process Python hooks, backend processes, lifecycle/install scripts, and openCommand. App code can access the filesystem, network, and in-memory credentials; enable this only for apps you trust (CSE SEC-012). Prefer apps_trusted, which grants the same admission to ONE named app.

entries.label: Trusted Apps
entries.help: Per-app grants for third-party execution — the narrow form of apps_allow_third_party. An app whose manifest name appears here is admitted to run Python hooks, its backend, lifecycle scripts, and openCommand; every other third-party app stays blocked. Only a JSON array of app-name strings is honoured, and no wildcard entry is accepted (use apps_allow_third_party to trust all).

entries.label: Jail
entries.help: Process-isolation jail mode for agent-bearing commands. 'auto' uses a jail when the active edition supplies a working backend (the public edition has none, so 'auto' and 'on' are no-ops there); 'off' disables it. Disable per-invocation with --no-jail or KIROCREW_NO_JAIL=1.

entries.label: Dangerously Skip Permissions
entries.help: Skip EVERY tool approval confirmation, permanently. Declaring it here is a standing instruction: the grant does not expire and is re-established on every startup. This is the advanced, config-file-only escape hatch — there is deliberately no dashboard toggle for it. An enterprise policy can forbid it, which falls back to the ad-hoc duration below.

entries.label: Ad-hoc Auto-approve Duration
entries.help: How long auto-approve (YOLO) lasts when it is enabled AD HOC — from the dashboard picker, Slack, or the API. Every one of those surfaces uses this same duration. Accepts 30m / 1h / 6h / 12h / 24h, or until_shutdown to keep it on with no timed expiry until Kiro Crew restarts. Timed values are capped at 24h. Does NOT apply to a grant declared via 'dangerously_skip_permissions' above, which persists.

entries.label: Notify on Override Expiry
entries.help: DM the Slack owner when a time-limited safety override (YOLO) expires. Disable to silence the recurring expiry DM; the dashboard banner still shows.

entries.label: Bot Name
entries.help: Custom name the bot identifies as in conversations. Leave empty for default.

entries.label: Conductor Skill
entries.help: Enable agent delegation — loads conductor skill with agent roster.

entries.label: MCP Tool Search
entries.help: Load MCP tool specs on demand (search-and-call) instead of sending every tool definition each turn, keeping the context window clear when many MCP servers are configured. kiro-cli backend only. When enabled, Kiro Crew forces deferral always-on (minPct=0/minTokens=0) via the per-session kiro settings overlay; disabling reverts to sending full tool specs. No effect on an alternate ACP backend.

entries.label: Session Sharing
entries.help: Subagents reuse a shared ACP runtime instead of spawning a fresh kiro-cli process per subagent. Reduces startup from ~3-5s to ~200ms and memory from ~400MB to near-zero per subagent. Default ON for the kiro-cli backend; always off / ignored for an alternate ACP backend (which uses AcpClient). Set false to opt kiro back onto per-subagent processes.

entries.label: Max SubAgents
entries.help: Maximum amount of subagents at one time. 0 = auto-size the cap at startup from host memory/CPU and a learned per-agent cost (see dynamic-subagent-sizing docs). Default; set a fixed cap by pinning an integer >= 3 (values of 1 or 2 are raised to 3 — a pin below 3 would disable auto-sizing and run under the default).

entries.label: Spawn Min Memory GB
entries.help: Minimum available memory (GB) required to spawn a subagent. 0 disables the check.

entries.label: Resource Pressure Threshold (GB)
entries.help: Available memory (GB) at or below which the agent is told host memory is 'tight' via a compact [RESOURCES] context line, so it can prefer the lighter path for heavy work (targeted tests, smaller sub-agent waves). Advisory only — not enforced. 0 disables the context line. Lower this on small-memory hosts / memory-limited containers (e.g. a 2-4 GB pod) so the advisory only fires under genuine pressure.

entries.label: Resource Critical Threshold (GB)
entries.help: Available memory (GB) at or below which the [RESOURCES] context line escalates to 'critically low' and advises against starting heavy work at all. Should be <= resource_pressure_gb. 0 disables the critical tier.

entries.label: Workflow Run Timeout (secs)
entries.help: Wall-clock ceiling for one dynamic-workflow run. This is a runaway backstop, so it is clamped to 60s..21600s (6h) — raise it for long multi-phase investigations, but it can never be disabled. Reaching the ceiling is no longer a data-loss event: every agent result completed before the cutoff is preserved on the run record.

entries.label: SubAgent Memory Buffer %
entries.help: Percent of available memory and CPU reserved for the OS and other processes when auto-sizing the subagent cap (max_subagents=0).

entries.label: Chat Turn Timeout (secs)
entries.help: Wall-clock ceiling for one chat turn. This is a runaway backstop, so it is clamped to 300s..7200s (2h) and can never be disabled. Long babysit and monitoring turns approach the default, so hitting it is no longer silent: the turn ends with a visible card naming the limit. Values above the ACP transport's own prompt timeout are clamped, because the transport bounds the turn first.

entries.label: SubAgent Memory Cost (GB)
entries.help: First-boot per-agent memory-cost fallback (GB) used to auto-size the cap until a learned value accumulates.

entries.label: SubAgent CPU Cost (cores)
entries.help: First-boot per-agent CPU-cost fallback (cores) used to auto-size the cap until a learned value accumulates.

entries.label: SubAgent Auto-Size Max
entries.help: Ceiling on the auto-sized subagent cap (only applies when max_subagents=0). Stands in for the LLM-provider concurrency limit the local memory/CPU formula does not model. Ignored when max_subagents is set explicitly.

entries.label: SubAgent Spawn Stagger (seconds)
entries.help: Delay between successive subagent spawns (initial fill and queued drain) to bound cold-start CPU/memory spikes.

entries.label: SubAgent Max Turns
entries.help: Default tool-call budget per subagent.

entries.label: SubAgent Timeout (seconds)
entries.help: Wall-clock timeout per subagent execution. 0 uses hardcoded default (1800s).

entries.label: SubAgent Stall Idle (seconds)
entries.help: Seconds with no stream activity before a running subagent is surfaced as 'stalled' in the running-card. 0 uses hardcoded default (120s).

entries.label: Completion Keep
entries.help: Which end of the subagent transcript to keep in the completion event injected into the parent session. Three values: 'head' (first N chars), 'tail' (last N chars), 'both' (head + middle marker + tail). The full transcript stays in result.txt until cleanup; use spawn_status MCP tool to read it.

entries.label: Completion Keep Chars
entries.help: Maximum characters retained in the completion event after applying completion_keep. 0 disables truncation entirely. Default 3000.

entries.label: SubAgent Result TTL (seconds)
entries.help: How long a delivered subagent's result.txt is retained before the reaper prunes it. The completion event returns a summary plus this file path; the parent reads the full transcript on demand (read / grep / spawn_status) within this window instead of re-running the subagent. 0 prunes on the next reaper sweep. Default 3600 (1h).

entries.label: SubAgent CWD Allowed Roots
entries.help: Directory roots under which spawn_run's cwd parameter is permitted. Values support ~ expansion. Empty list disables cwd overrides.

entries.label: Max Channels
entries.help: Maximum concurrent agent channels (1-5).

entries.label: Max Channel Agents
entries.help: Maximum agents per channel (1-10).

entries.label: Log Level
entries.help: Persistent log level for the kiro_crew logger. Applied at startup; overridden by --verbose CLI flag.

entries.label: Soft-Stop Budget
entries.help: Seconds to wait for cooperative cancel before hard-killing the session.

entries.label: Session
entries.help: Session management settings.

entries.label: Session Timeout
entries.help: Idle session timeout in seconds.

entries.label: Auto-Continue on Empty Response
entries.help: After the model returns an empty response twice in a row, automatically send one 'continue' nudge on the same session (transcript-visible, bounded to once per user message).

entries.label: Auto-Compact Threshold
entries.help: Context usage percentage at which auto-compaction triggers (5-90).

entries.label: Warm Pool Size
entries.help: Number of pre-spawned kiro-cli processes kept ready for instant session start. 0 disables.

entries.label: Warm Pool Agent
entries.help: Agent name for warm pool processes. Empty string uses agent.default_agent.

entries.label: Warm Pool TTL
entries.help: Max age in seconds for pooled processes. Stale processes are discarded at claim time. 0 disables.

entries.label: Archive Retention (days)
entries.help: Days to keep compacted/rotated session archives before auto-cleanup. -1 disables cleanup (manage deletion manually).

entries.label: Watchdog RSS Limit (MiB)
entries.help: Recycle a session when its process tree resident memory exceeds this many MiB. 0 disables (default). Busy sessions (turn in flight) are never recycled.

entries.label: Task Runner
entries.help: Task runner configuration.

entries.label: Max Parallel Steps
entries.help: Maximum task steps to run in parallel. 0 = auto (the host-safe cap from agent.subagent_auto_max, clamped to memory/CPU). A positive value only *lowers* concurrency — it is capped at the auto maximum and can never exceed the host-safe limit.

entries.label: Workspace Folder
entries.help: Absolute path where task runner executions run. When set, every execution operates in this folder instead of a per-run scratch directory, so the task runner works on the intended target location. Empty = use the default per-run workspace directory.

entries.label: Orchestrator
entries.help: Autopilot/orchestrator settings.

entries.label: Stage Timeout
entries.help: Max seconds per stage before auto-run stops. Default 30 min.

entries.label: Messaging
entries.help: Channel-neutral messaging transport settings.

entries.label: Use Transport
entries.help: Route inbound Slack messages through the SlackTransport → TurnDriver → SlackRenderer channel-neutral path instead of the native handle_message monolith. Default ON in Kiro Crew (the transport abstraction is the canonical path, shared with future channels). Set to false to fall back to the legacy native handler.

entries.label: DM Session Scope
entries.help: How direct-message conversations map to sessions. 'per-channel-peer' (default) keeps one session per (channel, user), so the same person on Telegram vs WeCom stays isolated. 'unified' collapses all DMs into one shared session per agent for cross-surface continuity.

entries.label: DM Idle Reset (minutes)
entries.help: Start a fresh session generation when a DM arrives after this many minutes of inactivity. 0 (default) disables idle reset.

entries.label: DM Daily Reset Hour
entries.help: Local-time hour (0-23) at which the next DM starts a fresh session generation once per day. -1 (default) disables daily reset.

entries.label: DM Queue Mode
entries.help: How a DM that arrives while a turn is running is handled. 'steer' (default) folds it into the running reply; 'queue' holds it and runs it after the current turn finishes.

entries.label: Cron History
entries.help: Cron execution history storage limits.

entries.label: Summary Cap
entries.help: Max characters for run summary field.

entries.label: Trace Cap KB
entries.help: Max kilobytes for run trace field.

entries.label: Max Records Per Job
entries.help: Max history records kept per job file.

entries.label: Max Index Records
entries.help: Max records in the global index.

entries.label: Memory
entries.help: Memory and embedding configuration.

entries.label: Embedding Provider
entries.help: Vector embedding backend (always-on). In-process via vendored llama-cpp-python. Legacy configs with 'ollama' or 'none' are auto-migrated to 'llama_cpp'.

entries.label: Embedding Dimension
entries.help: Dimensionality of embedding vectors.

entries.label: Embedding Model URL
entries.help: Override HTTPS URL for the embedding model GGUF download (mirrored/airgapped deployments). Empty uses the public Kiro Crew CDN default; the KIROCREW_EMBED_MODEL_URL env var wins over both. The download is sha256-verified regardless of source.

entries.label: Embedding Model Path
entries.help: Absolute path to a local GGUF embedding model to use INSTEAD of the bundled Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B. When set, the default model is never downloaded or installed, so a custom model survives a default-model version change. Set embedding_dim to the model's output width. Changing the model changes the vector space, so stored embeddings are regenerated automatically. The KIROCREW_EMBED_MODEL_PATH env var wins over this.

entries.label: Embedding Model ID
entries.help: Optional stable identifier for a custom model's vector space. Defaults to 'custom:<filename>:<size>', which changes when a different model file is used. Set this explicitly if you swap between models of identical byte size, which the default derivation cannot distinguish.

entries.label: Semantic Confidence Threshold
entries.help: Minimum similarity score for semantic search results.

entries.label: Episodic Dedup Threshold
entries.help: Similarity threshold for deduplicating episodic memories.

entries.label: Episodic Max Results
entries.help: Maximum episodic memory results per query.

entries.label: Episodic Max Count
entries.help: Maximum total episodic memories stored.

entries.label: Semantic Keys
entries.help: Keys to index for semantic search.

entries.label: History Idle Hours
entries.help: Hours of inactivity before history consolidation.

entries.label: History Max Days
entries.help: Maximum days of history to retain.

entries.label: Migrated
entries.help: Whether memory has been migrated to vector store.

entries.label: Knowledge
entries.help: Knowledge Library ingestion settings.

entries.label: Auto-Ingest Artifacts
entries.help: Automatically ingest content-bearing local artifacts (markdown/text documents you save and iterate) into the Knowledge Library so they become searchable, keep them in sync as the artifact changes, and remove them from the Library when the artifact is deleted. They appear as a single aggregate 'Artifacts' source. On by default.

entries.label: Auto-Ingest Artifact Kinds
entries.help: Artifact kinds eligible for auto-ingest. Defaults to substantial document kinds (markdown, text, html, json); widget is excluded (UI/dashboards, not documents) and svg has no reader support.

entries.label: Max Ingest File Size (MB)
entries.help: Per-file size cap for Knowledge Library ingestion. Oversized files are skipped with a WARNING naming the file instead of being chunked -- chunking a very large file (e.g. a tens-of-MB CSV->MD conversion) is CPU-bound and previously hung gateway startup. Set 0 to disable the cap.

entries.label: Embed Timeout (seconds)
entries.help: Per-request timeout for the Knowledge-Library embedder. Raise it when a large chunk times out on a cold Ollama model load (the embed then never completes and the item is retried every maintenance pass). 0 or unset keeps the built-in 10s default.

entries.label: Embed Content Budget (chars)
entries.help: Safety bound (chars) on chunk content folded into an item embedding. 0 or unset keeps the built-in default (a generous backstop for pathological un-chunked input); raise/lower only to tune truncation.

entries.label: Pool Idle TTL (secs)
entries.help: Seconds the document-extraction worker pool may sit fully idle before it is scaled to zero (all workers shut down, freeing ~1GB of held process trees); the next ingest respawns them lazily. 0 keeps the workers warm indefinitely.

entries.label: Auto-Add Documents
entries.help: Let the agent add documents it comes across during normal work to the Knowledge Library, so they become searchable later. The agent reads the document with its own tools, under your approval, and hands over the text -- Kiro Crew fetches nothing itself, so the doc-ingest host allowlist below does not apply. Added documents appear in a single aggregate 'Auto-added' source you can remove in one click. On by default. Renamed from auto_ingest_doc_links, which is still accepted.

entries.label: Auto-Register Project Documents
entries.help: Register the documents of each project you work in as a Knowledge source automatically, so a project's design docs, specs and READMEs become searchable without adding the folder by hand. Only documents are taken (.md/.pdf/.docx/.org above a small size floor, excluding agent instructions, generated files and repository boilerplate) -- never source code. No confirmation step: the document filter and the per-sweep chunk budget below bound the cost, and deleting the source keeps it deleted. On by default.

entries.label: Auto-Ingest Chunk Budget
entries.help: Chunks an automatically-registered source may ingest per watcher sweep. Each chunk costs one LLM extraction call, so this is what actually bounds the cost of auto-registration -- file filters bound pollution, not spend. Newest documents land first and the rest trickle in on later sweeps, so a new project never arrives as a burst. 0 removes the bound.

entries.label: Folder Ingest Chunk Budget
entries.help: Chunks a folder you add by hand may ingest per watcher sweep. Adding a source-code repository discovers thousands of files, and each chunk costs an LLM extraction call on a pool of billed sessions, so an unpaced first scan can spend a large amount unattended. Nothing is skipped: newest files land first and the rest continue on later sweeps. Higher than the auto-ingest budget because you asked for the folder explicitly. 0 removes the bound; a per-source chunk_budget property overrides it for one folder.

entries.label: De-duplicate Every N Sweeps
entries.help: Run a full duplicate-collapsing pass every Nth watcher sweep. The per-write gate refuses a byte-identical document, but only a full pass catches a near-duplicate (the same document edited slightly between two sources) or duplicates that already existed. At the default 300s sweep interval, 12 is roughly hourly. 0 disables it.

entries.label: Doc-Ingest Host Allowlist
entries.help: Exact hostnames whose links may be fetched by KIROCREW ITSELF and ingested, for an edition that wires a server-side doc-link scanner. Empty = fetch nothing (SSRF-safe deny-by-default). This governs only that server-fetch path -- it does NOT gate 'Auto-Add Documents' above, where the agent has already fetched the content under its own approval and Kiro Crew fetches nothing. Applying it there would make the feature ingest nothing on a default config while its toggle reads on.

entries.label: Auto-Discover Documents Folder
entries.help: Watch for a documents folder inside the active workspace and register it as a Knowledge source automatically, so files dropped there become searchable without adding the source by hand. The folder is never created for you: its absence means you have not opted in, and it is picked up within one watcher sweep of being created -- no restart needed. Off by default because ingestion spends LLM extraction on every supported file in the folder.

entries.label: Documents Folder Name
entries.help: Name of the folder inside the workspace that auto-discovery looks for. A single path segment -- separators and traversal are rejected so the source cannot be redirected outside the workspace. Avoid 'knowledge': that is where the Library's own SQLite store lives and it always exists, which would defeat discovery.

entries.label: Skills
entries.help: Skill loading and matching configuration.

entries.label: Max Triggered
entries.help: Maximum number of skills a single message may flag as relevant (≥0). Each match injects that skill's full content, unless the skill sets inject_on_trigger: false (pointer-only; requires max_triggered > 0 to have any effect). Defaults to 0 (disabled): the agent discovers skills from the Available Skills index and reads them on demand via cat, $skillname, or skill_search. Set to a positive integer to re-enable per-turn word-overlap trigger matching.

entries.label: Lazy Skill Injection
entries.help: When true, the session-start skills block injects only a usage-ranked top-K of on-demand skills (bounded by its own section budget) and leaves the long tail discoverable via the skill_search tool / $skillname / triggers; each context section also gets its own independent char cap so the global ceiling becomes their sum (~190k) and a large skills set can never crowd out memory/lessons. Disabled by default (0-impact upgrade, like prewarm_count=0): off means the legacy full skills dump under a single shared 165k budget — unchanged behavior.

entries.label: Auto-Create Skills
entries.help: When true, analyze each session after completion and synthesize a reusable SKILL.md when a non-trivial multi-step procedure is detected. Candidates are staged for review (see approval_required) rather than going live, and live under skills/auto/ so they never collide with hand-authored skills. Disabled by default; enable in Settings → Skills.

entries.label: Auto-Refine Skills
entries.help: When true, update an existing auto-created skill if the agent succeeds via a different tool sequence than documented. Requires auto_create_from_sessions. Disabled by default.

entries.label: Auto Min Tool Calls
entries.help: Minimum tool calls in a session for it to qualify for skill extraction (≥2). Lower values produce more skills but reduce quality.

entries.label: Auto Similarity Threshold
entries.help: Skip creation when an existing skill's description has keyword overlap ≥ this fraction with the synthesized description (0.0-1.0). Prevents near-duplicate skills. Used as the lexical fallback when the Haiku dedupe judge is unavailable.

entries.label: Skill Approval Required
entries.help: When true, auto-generated skill candidates land in a pending queue for human review instead of going live. Prose-only skills may auto-publish when this is false; skills that bundle scripts ALWAYS require approval regardless of this flag.

entries.label: Max Auto Skills
entries.help: Hard cap (backstop) on the number of live auto-generated skills. When exceeded, the least-valuable (by recency + frequency) are archived — never hard-deleted — down to the cap (≥1).

entries.label: Skill Stale After (days)
entries.help: An auto-skill with no recorded use for this many days is marked stale (≥1). Never-used skills younger than this window are exempt (grace floor).

entries.label: Skill Archive After (days)
entries.help: An auto-skill inactive for this many days is archived (recoverable, never deleted). Must be ≥ stale_after_days.

entries.label: Pending Skill TTL (days)
entries.help: Unapproved skill candidates older than this are auto-cleaned from the pending queue (≥1).

entries.label: Generate Skill Scripts
entries.help: When true, deterministic procedures may generate a validated Python helper script alongside the SKILL.md. Script-bearing skills always require approval.

entries.label: Skill Judge Model
entries.help: Model used for the dedupe judge and the advisory pending review. Defaults to "auto" to inherit the account's governed model; the value only gates whether the judge runs (any truthy value enables it) — the judge turn itself runs on the shared background session.

entries.label: Extra Skill Paths
entries.help: Additional directories to scan for skills. Supports ~ expansion. Skills from extra_paths are read-only (trigger matching + loading). Local ~/.kiro/crew/skills/ takes precedence for duplicate names.

entries.label: Telemetry
entries.help: Metrics telemetry (local-first JSONL sink). Off by default.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Main switch for Kiro Crew metrics telemetry. Off by default: metric call sites are no-ops and nothing is written. When on, a local-first JSONL sink under ~/.kiro/crew/metrics is enabled (no network egress).

entries.label: Local Metrics Dir
entries.help: Directory for local JSONL metric shards. Empty = ~/.kiro/crew/metrics. Supports ~ expansion.

entries.label: Export Interval (s)
entries.help: How often the local exporter flushes aggregated metrics to disk (>=1).

entries.label: Retention (days)
entries.help: Prune local JSONL metric shards older than this many days on each export cycle. 0 disables age-based pruning. Bounds on-disk telemetry growth (rec #14: bounded retention).

entries.label: Max Total Size (MB)
entries.help: Opportunistic directory budget for local metric shards. Closed shards are pruned oldest-first; protected active writers can temporarily exceed the budget. 0 disables the size cap (rec #14: bounded retention).

entries.label: OTLP Endpoint
entries.help: Opt-in OpenTelemetry OTLP/HTTP metrics endpoint (e.g. http://localhost:4318/v1/metrics). EMPTY = no network egress (default). When set, aggregated metrics are ALSO pushed to this collector in addition to the local JSONL sink; requires the kirocrew[otlp] package extra to be installed (rec #1: OTLP opt-in only, no egress by default).

entries.label: Anonymous Usage Beacon
entries.help: Anonymous daily heartbeat so maintainers can see how many copies are actively running, which versions are in use, and which distribution channels they came from. Sends EXACTLY five fields, at most once per day: a random installation id, app release (major.minor.patch only — build stamps are stripped), Python minor version, distribution channel, and a first-run bit. NEVER sends prompts, model output, file contents, paths, repo names, credentials, hostname, username, IP address, operating system, CPU architecture, release channel, or governance posture. Automatically suppressed in CI and for a non-default KIROCREW_HOME. Opt out with KIROCREW_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 or by turning this off; an enterprise policy can also pin it off via the capabilities.telemetry governance scope, which this switch cannot override. Independent of the 'enabled' switch above, which is local-only metrics collection and still never egresses.

entries.label: Beacon Endpoint
entries.help: HTTPS base URL that receives the anonymous heartbeat. EMPTY = no beacon is ever sent, regardless of the toggle above. Must be https:// (a plaintext heartbeat would reveal which hosts run this software to any on-path observer); a non-https value is cleared.

entries.label: STT
entries.help: Speech-to-text transcription settings.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable voice memo transcription.

entries.label: Provider
entries.help: STT provider.

entries.label: Whisper Path
entries.help: Path to whisper binary (auto-detected if empty).

entries.label: Model
entries.help: Whisper model size.

entries.label: MLX Model
entries.help: Hugging Face repo for the mlx_whisper model (mlx provider only).

entries.label: Device
entries.help: Computation device.

entries.label: Timeout
entries.help: Transcription timeout in seconds.

entries.label: Transcribe Region
entries.help: AWS region for Transcribe API.

entries.label: Transcribe Profile
entries.help: AWS profile for Transcribe API.

entries.label: Language Code
entries.help: Language for speech recognition (e.g. en-US, fr-FR, es-ES).

entries.label: Streaming
entries.help: Stream partial transcripts live to the dashboard input. Supported by the streaming providers only: `transcribe` (AWS, cloud) and `apple` (on-device, macOS 26+). The whisper/mlx CLIs have no partial-result channel.

entries.label: Semantic endpointing
entries.help: While streaming dictation, run a fast background model on each stable transcript segment to detect when you have finished a complete request, then auto-submit. Streaming providers only (transcribe, apple); off by default.

entries.label: Dictation Panel
entries.help: Show the animated dictation panel while recording instead of the thin status bar. Ignored when the browser lacks WebGL2 or the OS requests reduced motion — both fall back to the status bar.

entries.label: Computer Use
entries.help: Desktop automation tree/screenshot budgets. The primary enable is NOT here — it lives on the keystone computer_use.json.

entries.label: Max Tree Nodes
entries.help: Accessibility nodes one window walk may return before truncating.

entries.label: Max Tree Depth
entries.help: How deep one accessibility walk descends.

entries.label: Text Limit
entries.help: Characters kept per element title/value.

entries.label: Attach Screenshots
entries.help: Capture the target window and relay the image path alongside the tree. The accessibility tree is always the primary channel.

entries.label: Screenshot Width
entries.help: Longest edge of the downscaled screenshot, in pixels.

entries.label: Screenshot Quality
entries.help: JPEG quality 1-100 for the screenshot.

entries.label: Cursor Motion
entries.help: Draw a visible cursor gliding to each target before a real-pointer click, so the operator can see what the agent is doing. macOS only; purely visual and never a permit — the drawn cursor is not the pointer, and turning this on grants no new capability.

entries.label: MCP Gateway
entries.help: Sidecar MCP broker that shares backends across sessions.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Route MCP traffic through the shared sidecar broker. Default False — opt-in.

entries.label: Forward Declared Env
entries.help: Apply a pooled server's declared env (mcpServers.<name>.env) to the shared backend. Only non-secret keys are forwarded — rotating-secret and credential-prefixed keys are never applied to a shared backend. Default False — opt-in.

entries.label: Socket Path
entries.help: Local endpoint for the broker. Empty -> $KIROCREW_HOME/mcp-gateway/gateway.sock. A unix socket at this path on POSIX; on Windows the path is not created, it only derives the named-pipe name and locates the lock file beside it.

entries.label: Overlay Dir
entries.help: Directory of rewritten agent JSON. Broker stubs from these specs are injected into each kiro-cli session via ACP session/new. Empty -> $KIROCREW_HOME/mcp-gateway/agents.

entries.label: Idle Timeout
entries.help: Seconds a refcount=0 MCP backend is kept before drain.

entries.label: Max Backends
entries.help: Max concurrent pooled MCP backends before the pool refuses a new one. Must be >= the number of distinct (agent x server) backends that can be live at once: each agent keeps its own backend per server, so N concurrent agents with ~S servers each need N*S slots. Bounded by design: idle backends drain after idle_timeout_secs, so steady-state RAM tracks real concurrency, not this ceiling.

entries.label: Poolable Servers
entries.help: MCP server names allowed to share a pooled backend across sessions. A stdio server is pooled when its name appears here OR its agent-JSON entry sets poolable:true. Safe by default — non-listed servers run per-session. Managed from Settings -> Shared MCP gateway.

entries.label: Prewarm Count
entries.help: Number of hottest observed (agent x server x channel) MCP backends to spawn at gateway startup, before the first session connects. Removes the cold-start latency on the first new-chat after a gateway restart or after all backends have idled out — the steady state already reuses warm backends within the idle timeout. The hot set is learned from prior registers and persisted beside the socket; channel_id is a stable id, so a prewarmed backend is reused by every later new-chat in that channel. 0 (default) disables prewarming — no hot-key file is read or written.

entries.label: Read Buffer Limit
entries.help: Maximum bytes for a single MCP response line before asyncio drops it. Default 64 MiB. Responses exceeding this are fast-failed with -32000. Env override: KIROCREW_MCP_READ_LIMIT.

entries.label: Response Spill Threshold
entries.help: Tool-call responses larger than this (bytes) have their text content written to ~/.kiro/crew/mcp_spill/ and truncated inline to 16 KiB + a file path marker. Default 256 KiB. Set 0 to disable spilling. Env override: KIROCREW_MCP_SPILL_THRESHOLD.

entries.label: Instances
entries.help: Multi-instance management — manage/switch remote Kiro Crews over SSH.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable multi-instance management — lets this gateway open SSH tunnels to remote Kiro Crews and embed their dashboards. Default off (opt-in). Enabling also scopes a CSP frame-src relaxation to active tunnel ports.

entries.label: Warm Set Cap
entries.help: Max number of remote instances kept warm (iframe mounted + tunnel live) at once. Least-recently-used instances beyond this are evicted and reconnected on demand. Bounds memory/socket use (each warm instance is a full dashboard SPA).

entries.label: Tunnel Base Port
entries.help: First local loopback port used for an SSH -L forward. The allocator increments from here, skipping ports already in use.

entries.label: SSH Compression
entries.help: Enable SSH transport compression (ssh -C) on instance tunnels. The remote dashboard SPA bundle plus all API/WebSocket traffic travel over this forwarded stream and are highly compressible; the gateway does not gzip HTTP responses, so this is the only compression in the path. Default on (best for a dedicated remote host over a slow link); turn off on a fast/local link where compression CPU outweighs the bandwidth win.

entries.label: Max Recovery Attempts
entries.help: Consecutive self-heal attempts before a dropped tunnel is left disconnected. With the capped-exponential backoff, the default 8 spans a ~2 min recovery window, enough to outlast a transient drop (screen lock, proxy warmup) before giving up.

entries.label: Recover Backoff Cap (secs)
entries.help: Cap on the per-attempt backoff between self-heal attempts. The wait grows 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 then holds at this cap; raising it spaces retries further across a slow reconnect.

entries.label: Probe Failure Threshold
entries.help: Consecutive health-probe failures before a connected-but-not-forwarding (zombie) tunnel is torn down to trigger self-heal.

entries.label: Heartbeat
entries.help: Heartbeat background task queue delivery defaults.

entries.label: Default delivery
entries.help: Where a heartbeat completion with no inline <!-- deliver:... --> tag is routed: 'slack' (Slack DM + dashboard bell, the default) or 'dashboard' (dashboard slot + bell only, no Slack). Per-task deliver tags always override this.

entries.label: Watchdog
entries.help: ACP per-session watchdog / liveness-oracle windows.

entries.label: Check after (s)
entries.help: Idle seconds on a turn before the liveness oracle is consulted at all. Below this, the dispatch loop does no watchdog work.

entries.label: Stale probe window (s)
entries.help: Idle seconds before an UNKNOWN-verdict model-wait turn is safe-probed via session/cancel. Probes are non-lethal: a live turn auto-recovers.

entries.label: Tool stall suspect (s)
entries.help: Idle seconds before an UNKNOWN-verdict in-flight tool is cancelled and the turn routed to tool-stall recovery (continue-nudge, no re-run of the original message). WORKING tools (e.g. a matched live build child) are never cancelled regardless of duration. Default 3h to accommodate long-running builds and MCP tools on macOS where the liveness oracle degrades (no /proc) and cannot distinguish live builds from stalls.

entries.label: Hard cap (s)
entries.help: Absolute ceiling for UNKNOWN-verdict forbearance (e.g. the extended probably-thinking window). Applies ONLY to UNKNOWN verdicts — never to a WORKING session. Default 3h.

entries.label: Silent-think probe window (s)
entries.help: Extended probe window for a model-wait with an established backend connection but flat counters (non-streamed server-side reasoning, e.g. long xhigh thinks). Probing a live think cancels and regenerates it, so this window is deliberately generous.

entries.label: Wellness sample interval (s)
entries.help: Minimum spacing between CPU/IO counter samples used for movement deltas in the liveness oracle.

entries.label: Slack
entries.help: Slack integration settings.

entries.label: Allowed Users
entries.help: List of Slack users allowed to interact. Each entry: {slack_id, name}.

entries.label: Tracking Channels
entries.help: Slack channels to monitor. Each entry: {channel_id, name}.

entries.label: Open Channels
entries.help: Channel IDs where all users are authorized without allowlist.

entries.label: Command
entries.help: Slack slash command trigger word.

entries.label: Forward to Agent Callback
entries.help: Callback ID for the 'Forward to Agent' message shortcut. Must match the callback_id configured in your Slack app manifest. Leave empty to disable the feature.

entries.label: Trusted Bot IDs
entries.help: Bot IDs allowed to bypass the bot filter for multi-node mesh communication.

entries.label: Allowed Enterprise IDs
entries.help: Slack Enterprise Grid org IDs to allow. Empty list allows all orgs (default-open).

entries.label: Reactions
entries.help: Override phase reaction emojis. Valid keys: queued, thinking, coding, browsing, tool, done, error. Set a value to null to suppress that phase entirely.

entries.label: Reactions Enabled
entries.help: Show phase-aware emoji reactions on Slack messages during processing.

entries.label: Show Thinking
entries.help: Post the model's thinking/reasoning as a thread reply in Slack. Disable to keep responses concise.

entries.label: Home Tab Sessions Per Kind
entries.help: Max sessions shown per category (main chat / autopilot) in the Slack Home Tab.

entries.label: Use Tunnel URL in Slack
entries.help: When true, dashboard links posted to Slack (e.g. via /kirocrew dashboard) use the tunnel URL if one is active. When false (default), Slack links always use the configured dashboard origin or host:port. Disabled by default until the tunnel mechanism is scaled for general use.

entries.label: Publish
entries.help: Artifact publishing controls (destinations allowlist).

entries.label: Allowed Publish Destinations
entries.help: Publish-provider ids the operator permits (registry keys). Empty list allows all registered destinations (default-open). Cannot widen past the enterprise governance ceiling.

entries.label: Artifact Relocate Roots
entries.help: Extra absolute filesystem roots an artifact may be relocated into, beyond your home directory. Empty = home-only (the secure default). The sensitive-path denylist (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kiro/crew, …) still applies inside every allowed root.

entries.label: WeCom
entries.help: WeCom (企业微信) AI-bot integration settings.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable the WeCom channel via WeCom AI-bot. Requires the WECOM_BOT_ID and WECOM_SECRET credentials to be set.

entries.label: Allowed Users
entries.help: WeCom users allowed to DM the bot. Each entry: {userid, name}. The owner is always allowed.

entries.label: Allow All Users
entries.help: Let every member of the WeCom organization DM the bot, bypassing the allow-list. Safe-ish because a WeCom AI bot is reachable only inside your own org tenant (unlike globally addressable bots), but it grants agent access to the whole company. Default off.

entries.label: WebSocket URL
entries.help: WeCom AI-bot long-connection endpoint.

entries.label: Soft Context Threshold %
entries.help: When a DM's context passes this, prompt the user to /compact or /new instead of auto-compacting.

entries.label: Hard Context Threshold %
entries.help: Force a compaction when context reaches this, even without a user decision, so the window never overflows.

entries.label: Telegram
entries.help: Telegram Bot API integration settings.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable the Telegram Bot API channel (long-polling). Requires TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (env/.env) or telegram.bot_token.

entries.label: Bot Token
entries.help: Telegram Bot API token from @BotFather. Prefer the TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN credential (env/.env) over storing it here.

entries.label: Allowed User IDs
entries.help: Numeric Telegram user IDs permitted to DM the bot. Empty = deny all (fail closed): a Telegram bot is globally reachable by @username.

entries.label: Soft Context Threshold %
entries.help: Prompt the user to /compact or /new when context passes this percentage.

entries.label: Allow Forum Topics
entries.help: Serve Telegram supergroup forum Topics as per-topic sessions (Slack-thread style). Fail-closed: also requires the supergroup's chat_id in allowed_forum_chat_ids.

entries.label: Allowed Forum Chat IDs
entries.help: Numeric supergroup chat_ids permitted to run forum-topic sessions. Empty = deny all groups (fail closed).

entries.label: WeChat
entries.help: Weixin (iLink personal WeChat) integration settings.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable the Weixin (iLink personal WeChat) channel (long-polling). Requires a bot token + account id from the Settings QR flow.

entries.label: Bot Token
entries.help: iLink bot token (from QR login). Prefer the WEIXIN_TOKEN credential (env/.env / cred store) over storing it here.

entries.label: Account ID
entries.help: iLink bot account id captured during QR login.

entries.label: iLink Base URL
entries.help: iLink API base URL (per-account, returned by QR login).

entries.label: DM Policy
entries.help: Who may DM the bot: 'allowlist' (only allowed_user_ids, the default), 'open' (any sender), or 'disabled'. Defaults to allowlist with an empty list, so a freshly connected bot authorizes NOBODY until you add an id.

entries.label: Allowed User IDs
entries.help: Weixin user ids permitted to DM the bot when dm_policy='allowlist'. Empty = deny all (fail closed).

entries.label: Soft Context Threshold %
entries.help: Prompt the user to /compact or /new when context passes this percentage.

entries.label: Hard Context Threshold %
entries.help: Force a compaction when context passes this percentage.

entries.label: Discord
entries.help: Discord bot integration settings.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable the Discord channel (Gateway WebSocket, DMs plus optional allow-listed server threads). Requires DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN (env/.env) or discord.bot_token.

entries.label: Bot Token
entries.help: Discord bot token from the Developer Portal (Bot page). Prefer the DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN credential (env/.env) over storing it here.

entries.label: Allowed User IDs
entries.help: Discord user IDs (snowflakes) permitted to message the bot. Empty = deny all (fail closed).

entries.label: Allowed Thread IDs
entries.help: Discord server thread IDs where approved users may run the agent. Empty = DMs only. Normal server channels are always denied.

entries.label: Soft Context Threshold %
entries.help: Prompt the user to !compact or !new when context passes this percentage.

entries.label: Webex
entries.help: Webex Messaging integration settings.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable the Webex Messaging channel (device WebSocket, no public URL needed). Requires WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN (env/.env) or webex.bot_token.

entries.label: Bot Token
entries.help: Webex bot access token from developer.webex.com (My Webex Apps). Prefer the WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN credential (env/.env) over storing it here.

entries.label: Allowed Emails
entries.help: Webex account emails permitted to DM the bot. Empty = deny all (fail closed): anyone in the org can message a Webex bot.

entries.label: Soft Context Threshold %
entries.help: When a DM's context passes this, prompt the user to /compact or /new instead of auto-compacting.

entries.label: Hard Context Threshold %
entries.help: Force a compaction when context reaches this, even without a user decision, so the window never overflows.

entries.label: Teams
entries.help: Microsoft Teams integration settings.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable the Microsoft Teams channel (self-hosted inbound HTTPS webhook via the Bot Framework). Requires a public HTTPS endpoint pointing at /api/messaging/teams plus MICROSOFT_APP_ID and MICROSOFT_APP_PASSWORD (env/.env) or teams.app_id/app_password.

entries.label: App ID
entries.help: Microsoft App (Client) ID of the Azure Bot registration. Prefer the MICROSOFT_APP_ID credential (env/.env) over storing it here.

entries.label: App Password
entries.help: Azure Bot client secret. Set ONLY via the MICROSOFT_APP_PASSWORD credential (env/.env); it is deliberately NOT read from config.json so the agent-readable config never holds the secret.

entries.label: Tenant ID
entries.help: Azure AD tenant id for a single-tenant bot. Leave empty for a multi-tenant bot (uses the botframework.com token authority).

entries.label: Allowed Emails
entries.help: Azure AD UPNs/emails OR AAD object ids permitted to DM the bot. Teams activities reliably carry the sender's object id (email is often absent), so listing object ids works out of the box; emails are matched when Teams supplies them. Empty = deny all (fail closed): a Teams bot is reachable by anyone in the org.

entries.label: Soft Context Threshold %
entries.help: When a DM's context passes this, prompt the user to /compact or /new instead of auto-compacting.

entries.label: Hard Context Threshold %
entries.help: Force a compaction when context reaches this, even without a user decision, so the window never overflows.

entries.label: Dashboard
entries.help: Dashboard UI settings.

entries.label: Dashboard URL
entries.help: Public URL for the dashboard (used in Slack links).

entries.label: Tailscale
entries.help: Reach the dashboard over your tailnet via `tailscale serve`.

entries.label: Tailnet Access
entries.help: Accept this machine's own MagicDNS name as a dashboard origin, so `tailscale serve` works without hand-writing dashboard.url. Reads the local Tailscale daemon once at startup; contributes nothing if Tailscale is absent, stopped, or MagicDNS is off. Does NOT widen the network bind and does NOT change authentication — every request still needs a dashboard session.

entries.label: Restore Sessions
entries.help: Re-open recently active sessions on startup.

entries.label: Restore Window Minutes
entries.help: Time window (minutes) for session restoration, and for surfacing channel conversations in the chat list (0-1440). 0 = no limit.

entries.label: Show Channel Conversations In Chat List
entries.help: Show recently active Slack/Discord/Teams (etc.) conversations in the dashboard's chat list instead of only under History. Uses the same recency window as session restoration.

entries.label: Bot Name
entries.help: Custom bot display name for the dashboard UI.

entries.label: Avatar
entries.help: Path to custom avatar image for the dashboard UI.

entries.label: Merge Queued Messages
entries.help: Concatenate follow-up messages while the agent is busy instead of queueing them separately.

entries.label: MCP Probe Timeout
entries.help: Seconds to wait for MCP server handshake during probe (5-120).

entries.label: Loop-stall Hard-exit Budget (secs)
entries.help: Seconds the gateway's event loop may go silent before it dumps all thread stacks and exits so systemd can restart it. Raise it on a host that does heavy subprocess work (long builds, test suites, many child reaps), which can wedge the loop briefly without being genuinely dead. Clamped to 10s..300s. Note the desktop app's liveness probe kills at roughly 20s independently, so a value above that only takes effect for a headless gateway — the desktop probe wins first and the stack dump is lost.

entries.label: Widget Density
entries.help: How aggressively the agent uses inline widgets. 'more' encourages widgets for any visual content; 'less' limits to only when markdown is clearly insufficient.

entries.label: Response Verbosity
entries.help: Controls how terse the agent's prose is. 'default' is normal; 'concise' injects brevity guidelines (lead with the answer, cut filler, keep code/errors verbatim); 'ultra' writes for an ADHD reader — the answer lands in a 3-sentence opening, and any detail after it must be scannable bullets rather than prose. Both levels preserve full detail for security warnings, irreversible-action confirmations, and ordered multi-step instructions.

entries.label: Link Previews
entries.help: Render http(s) links in assistant messages as favicon + page title instead of a raw URL. Off by default because it is a network decision, not a display one: this machine fetches every link the model outputs, so each linked site sees a request from your IP address. When false the /api/link-meta endpoint fetches nothing and returns 403.

entries.label: Spend Credits To Read The Credit Meter
entries.help: Let the credit pill fall back to a `kiro-cli /usage` chat turn when the free usage API returns no plan. That fallback is a REAL billed LLM turn on whichever model the lite agent resolves, and it repeats on every refresh interval for as long as any dashboard tab is open, so it is off by default: a meter that reports spending must not itself spend. While it is off the pill shows whatever the free API returned and hides when the API has nothing to show.

entries.label: Tail-only Fork
entries.help: When forking, keep only the messages after the chosen point. The earlier messages are dropped.

entries.label: Auto Open Browser
entries.help: Open the dashboard URL in the default browser on gateway startup.

entries.label: Prevent Sleep While Running
entries.help: Keep this computer awake while the agent is running a task, so a long task is not interrupted by the machine going to sleep. Off by default. Uses caffeinate on macOS, systemd-inhibit on Linux, and SetThreadExecutionState on Windows; on a host with no keep-awake backend it is a no-op.

entries.label: Quick Send
entries.help: Click a suggested reply to send it instantly. Shift+Click to select multiple.

entries.label: Session Grid (Split View)
entries.help: Opt-in: enable terminal-style split view to run multiple chat sessions side by side.

entries.label: Open MCP Apps in the side panel
entries.help: Render interactive MCP Apps (such as Excalidraw diagrams) in the right side panel instead of inline in the chat bubble. The panel opens automatically and can be expanded; the chat keeps a compact placeholder linking to it.

entries.label: Terminal
entries.help: Terminal panel configuration. Set enabled=false to hide the CLI panel in the dashboard.

entries.label: Default Project
entries.help: Directory path used as the project for new chat tabs. Empty = workspace dir.

entries.label: Theme Mode
entries.help: Dashboard color mode preference: 'dark', 'light', or 'system'. Empty = unset (frontend falls back to localStorage or 'system').

entries.label: SSO Login Flags
entries.help: Flags passed to the SSO login command by an edition that supplies a real login handler (DashboardContributor.sso_login_handler). Empty = the edition default. Inert in the public build (the core /api/sso-login is a no-op stub); the companion validates the token allowlist when it uses them.

entries.label: Theme Color
entries.help: Dashboard color theme slug (e.g. 'kiro', 'emerald', 'monokai'). Empty = unset (frontend falls back to localStorage or 'kiro').

entries.label: Language
entries.help: Dashboard UI language as a BCP-47 tag (e.g. 'en', 'zh-CN'). Empty = auto-detect from the browser's preferred languages, falling back to English. Persisted here (not only in the browser) so the choice follows the user across browsers and the desktop app.

entries.label: Recent Session Tint Count
entries.help: Number of most-recently-active sessions to highlight in the sidebar with a graded accent stripe (0-10; 0 = off).

entries.label: Onboarded
entries.help: Whether the user has completed the dashboard onboarding flow. When true, the 'Choose your look' modal is skipped on first load.

entries.label: Import Onboarded
entries.help: Whether the user has completed or skipped foreign-agent import onboarding.

entries.label: Privacy Acknowledged
entries.help: Whether the user has seen the mandatory first-run Privacy chapter, which discloses the anonymous heartbeat and offers the opt-out. Server-backed rather than browser-local because the gateway gates the very FIRST heartbeat on it: until this is true the user has not yet been shown the opt-out, and a ping sent before the offer makes the offer meaningless.

entries.label: User Role
entries.help: The user's professional background, collected during onboarding (developer, designer, product-manager, data-ml, it-ops, other). Injected into the agent prompt so responses match the user's domain vocabulary. Empty = unspecified.

entries.label: User Role (Custom)
entries.help: Free-text role the user typed when they picked 'other' during onboarding (e.g. 'solutions architect'). Consulted ONLY while user_role == 'other'; quoted verbatim into the agent prompt. Retained (not cleared) when another role is picked, so it is inert rather than contradictory and survives switching back. Empty = 'other' contributes nothing.

entries.label: User Technical Level
entries.help: How technical the user is (codes, somewhat-technical, non-technical), collected during onboarding. Injected into the agent prompt to calibrate explanation depth. Empty = unspecified.

entries.label: Tips Enabled
entries.help: Show feature tip cards while the agent is thinking.

entries.label: Folder Suggestions Enabled
entries.help: Offer to file a newly-titled, unfiled chat session into a matching folder.

entries.label: Tips Cadence Hours
entries.help: Minimum hours between showing a new tip.

entries.label: Tips Snooze Hours
entries.help: Hours before a snoozed tip becomes eligible again.

entries.label: Tips Recency Decay
entries.help: Decay factor for weighted-random selection (0-1). Lower = stronger bias to newer tips.

entries.label: Tips Model
entries.help: Model ID for tips generation. Defaults to "auto" so it inherits the account's governed model; a hardcoded id can be rejected on accounts or partitions that do not serve it.

entries.label: Tips Explore Ratio
entries.help: Probability of picking a random catalog tip instead of personalized (0-1). Higher = more general discovery.

entries.label: Self-Hosted GitLab Hosts
entries.help: Exact hostnames (optionally host:port) of self-managed GitLab instances whose merge-request URLs the Changes panel may load. Empty = gitlab.com only (deny-by-default): a merge-request URL is only sent to the glab CLI if its host is an exact member of this list, so a pasted link cannot aim the credential-bearing CLI at an arbitrary or internal host. Suffixes and wildcards are not matched. Adding an entry authorizes the local glab CLI, with its token, to reach that host, including hosts only resolvable on your network.

entries.label: Tunnel
entries.help: AEA tunnel settings for remote dashboard access.

entries.label: Enabled
entries.help: Enable a tunnel to expose the dashboard for remote access.

entries.label: Name Mode
entries.help: Tunnel naming: 'username' uses 'kirocrew', 'hash' uses 'kirocrew-<hostHash>' for multi-host disambiguation.

entries.label: Name Override
entries.help: Explicit tunnel name (overrides name_mode). Note: some tunnel providers prefix your username (e.g. 'foo' becomes '<user>-foo').

entries.label: Hooks
entries.help: Script hook definitions keyed by hook ID.

entries.label: Slack Channels
entries.help: Per-channel activation config.

entries.label: Activation
entries.help: Channel activation mode.

entries.label: Agent
entries.help: Agent override for this channel (empty = default).

entries.label: Thread Follow
entries.help: Respond to all messages in threads where bot was previously @mentioned.

entries.label: Slack DM Activation
entries.help: Default activation mode for DMs.

entries.label: Observe Max Messages
entries.help: Max messages per observe-mode channel.

entries.label: Observe TTL Hours
entries.help: Hours to keep observe history.

entries.label: Agents
entries.help: Named Kiro Crew agent definitions.

entries.label: Kiro Agent
entries.help: Kiro agent name (modeId for session/set_mode).

entries.label: Workspace
entries.help: Named workspace from the workspaces section.

entries.label: Memory Store
entries.help: Named memory store from the memory_stores section.

entries.label: Model
entries.help: Default model for sessions on this agent. Empty inherits: the bound kiro agent's own pinned model first, then the global agent.model fallback. A per-session pick still overrides this.

entries.label: Description
entries.help: Human-readable agent description.

entries.label: Triggers
entries.help: Routing intent for orchestrator crew selection: free-text 'when to use this crew' guidance the main agent reads via select_crew. A crew with no triggers is not offered for selection.

entries.label: Source
entries.help: Agent origin: kirocrew or builtin.

entries.label: Default Agent
entries.help: Active Kiro Crew agent name from the agents section.

entries.label: Workspaces
entries.help: Named workspace definitions.

entries.label: Directory
entries.help: Workspace directory path.

entries.label: Default Workspace
entries.help: Active workspace name.

entries.label: Memory Stores
entries.help: Named memory store definitions.

entries.label: Description
entries.help: Human-readable purpose of this memory store.

entries.label: Embedding Provider
entries.help: Override embedding backend for this store. Empty inherits from top-level memory (embeddings are always-on; per-store disable is not supported).

entries.label: Default Memory Store
entries.help: Fallback memory store name.

entries.label: Auto Update
entries.help: Enable automatic update checks.

entries.label: Timezone
entries.help: IANA timezone name (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'). Used to display cron schedules in local time.

entries.label: Snapshot Directory
entries.help: Directory for kirocrew snapshot output. Defaults to ~/.kiro/crew/snapshots if empty.

entries.label: Registries
entries.help: External app registries (org-owned repos). Each entry: {name, repo, branch}.

entries.label: Name
entries.help: Human-readable registry name (e.g. 'identityservices').

entries.label: Repo
entries.help: Git URL of the repo containing apps (https or ssh).

entries.label: Branch
entries.help: Git branch to read from.
